data.summary: The eight‑week schedule balances new content with practice, using the live classes when they align with the topics. Each week the student spends the full 6 hours on focused study, problem sets, and short quizzes, ending with a mixed review in the final week to consolidate knowledge before the exam.

tasks: Watch the live class (ID 10300) and take notes on Scalars/Vectors and Displacement/Velocity/Acceleration.
Complete the textbook problems for 1.1 and 1.2 (10 problems each).
Do 5 free‑response questions on representing motion (1.3) and check answers with the scoring guide.
Create a one‑page cheat sheet summarizing reference frames and relative motion (1.4).

weeks.focus: Force, free‑body diagrams, and Newton's laws
tasks: Read the unit chapter on forces and draw free‑body diagrams for 8 different scenarios.
Solve 12 problems covering Newton's First, Second, and Third Laws.
Complete a 15‑minute timed quiz on systems and center of mass (2.1).
Review solutions and write a one‑sentence explanation for each law.
Attend live class (ID 10301) covering Translational Kinetic Energy and Conservation of Energy.
Do the class worksheet: 8 problems on 3.1 and 6 problems on 3.4.
Complete textbook exercises on Work (3.2) and Power (3.5) – 5 problems each.
Create a concept map linking kinetic, potential, and total energy.
Read the momentum unit and summarize the impulse‑momentum theorem in 3 bullet points.
Solve 10 problems on linear momentum conservation, including one elastic and one inelastic collision.
Run a 20‑minute timed free‑response set covering 4.2 and 4.3.
Check answers against the scoring guide and note any mistakes.
Watch a short video on rotational kinematics and take notes on angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration.
Complete 8 problems linking linear and rotational motion (5.2).
Do 6 torque problems (5.3) and 4 rotational inertia calculations (5.4).
Summarize the key equations on a flash‑card sheet.

weeks.focus: Energy and momentum of rotating systems
tasks: Read the chapter on rotational kinetic energy and torque work; write a one‑paragraph explanation of each.
Solve 5 problems on rotational kinetic energy (6.1) and 5 on torque‑work (6.2).
Complete a set of 6 angular momentum and impulse questions (6.3).
Do a short practice test on conservation of angular momentum (6.4).
Read the SHM unit and derive the formulas for period and frequency.
Work through 8 problems on defining SHM and calculating period/frequency.
Analyze 5 oscillator graphs and write a brief interpretation for each (7.3).
Calculate the energy of 4 simple harmonic oscillators (7.4).
Take a 60‑minute full‑length AP Physics 1 practice exam (mixed units).
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide; record which topics lost points.
Do a targeted review: 2 problems each from the lowest‑scoring topics.
Create a final one‑page summary sheet covering formulas from all units.

data.final_week_advice: After the mixed review, focus on your weakest question types, redo those problems without notes, and keep a calm, timed routine for the actual exam day.
